bull.t: Accelerating platform growth and customer expansion
bull.b: Strong consumption growth, higher retention and expanding large-customer cohorts support durable revenue compounding. These trends indicate Snowflake is increasing workloads and share of customer data budgets rather than relying only on new-logo sales.

bull.t: AI and ecosystem expansion strengthen platform relevance
bull.b: Native AI adoption can increase platform consumption while broad cloud and software partnerships extend distribution. Embedding AI, data sharing and application connectivity may deepen customer reliance on Snowflake over multiple planning cycles.

bull.t: Positive cash generation and improving operating leverage
bull.b: Substantial cash generation gives Snowflake resources to fund product development, partnerships and buybacks while reducing dependence on external capital. Rising operating margins also suggest scale benefits can emerge as growth continues.

bear.t: Persistent GAAP losses and high operating expense intensity
bear.b: Snowflake’s attractive gross economics have not yet translated into GAAP profitability. Continued spending on sales, research and AI infrastructure could delay earnings maturity and limit resilience if growth slows or customers moderate consumption.

A more debt-heavy capital structure alongside ongoing losses reduces financial flexibility and increases sensitivity to execution setbacks. Although the balance sheet is not distressed, leverage may constrain investment choices if cash generation weakens.

bear.t: AI scaling may pressure margins and customer consumption
bear.b: AI is strategically important but may dilute platform economics if infrastructure costs outpace pricing or efficiency gains. Customer usage limits could also slow consumption growth, creating a lasting risk to both revenue expansion and margin improvement.
